title: Most Reformed join fiducia to faith; Rome distinguishes absolute faith but includes fiducia in living faith
source_text: LXIX. Vicissim vero Reformati plerique applicationem istam ad fiduciam pertinere non negant, sed ideo contendunt illam esse fidei actum, quod fiduciam cum fide conjungant, & fidei partem facere existiment. Nam sunt quidem inter Reformatos qui fiduciam a fide distinguunt, & fiduciam non fidei partem, sed effectum esse sentiunt; at Reformatorum plurimi fiduciam inter actus & partes fidei numerant, & per fiduciam fidem definiunt, tanquam per id quod est in ea praecipuum. Doctores autem Ecclesiae Romanae communi consensu pertendunt fiduciam esse a fide distinguendam, nec illam fidei partem aut actum constituere. Verum dum sic docent, fidem considerant simpliciter & absolute, & prout a fide tam viva quam mortua praescindit: sed si quis fidem ut vivam consideret, hoc respectu non negant, imo expresse docent, fiduciam fide includi, ut liquet ex iis quae supra citavimus.
pass_a_gloss: Conversely most of the Reformed do not deny that that application pertains to trust, but they contend it is an act of faith because they join trust with faith and judge it to make a part of faith. For there are indeed among the Reformed those who distinguish trust from faith and think trust is not a part of faith but an effect; but the majority of the Reformed number trust among the acts and parts of faith, and define faith by trust as by what is principal in it. But the Doctors of the Roman Church by common consent maintain that trust is to be distinguished from faith, and that it does not constitute a part or act of faith. Yet when they so teach, they consider faith simply and absolutely, and as it is prescinded from living as well as dead faith: but if anyone considers faith as living, in that respect they do not deny, indeed they expressly teach, that trust is included in faith, as is clear from what we cited above.
pass_b_english: Most Reformed admit application belongs to fiducia yet call it a faith-act because they join fiducia to faith; a minority treat fiducia as effect only.
Rome distinguishes fiducia from absolute faith, but expressly includes fiducia in living faith.

rejected: Rome excludes fiducia from living faith
